subject: Emergency personnel continuity and HC freeze waiver request - Acme Health pilot
messages:
From: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@acmehealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: temporary coverage for Acme pilot onboarding

Hi Karthik,

Quick note from Acme HR — our pilot for the Redwood integration is moving up by two weeks and we just had a senior security reviewer unexpectedly take a 6-week leave (medical). That reviewer was the only person trained on our internal onboarding checklist. We need a short-term SME to keep the pilot timeline (week of Mar 22) or we risk slipping the go-live and associated procurement milestone.

Can Redwood provide a temporary engineer or approve a short-term contractor for 6 weeks? We understand you have a company hiring freeze; Procurement asked me to surface a waiver or emergency exception if that makes sense on your side.

Attachments: current-onboarding-checklist.pdf (Acme internal), expected-coverage-gap.csv

Thanks,
Natalie Chen
Head of People Ops, Acme Health
Natalie.Chen@acmehealth.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: temporary coverage for Acme pilot onboarding

Team — looping you in. Acme is asking for a 6-week SME to preserve their pilot start date; they flagged procurement and the HC freeze. Quick summary:
- Impact: missing pilot will push contract signature and $120k in ARR to Q3 (Acme estimate).
- Need: single senior engineer with security onboarding experience for ~6 weeks, full-time on customer site/remote as contractor.
- Timing: start ~Mar 15-22.

Options I see: (1) repurpose a current IC on a noncritical infra project for a short stretch, (2) approve a contractor headcount under a waiver, (3) offer a limited-engagement from our Professional Services bench (if available).

Laura — can you advise on waiver path + escalation? Marissa — quick sense of cost / temporary budget hit? Grace/Rishi — is there an engineering contingency we should consider (on-call swap or reprioritize work)?

I'll forward Acme's checklist. This thread will live in my mailbox; please reply with quick decisions so I can get back to Natalie before EOD.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: temporary coverage for Acme pilot onboarding

Karthik — thanks for escalating. I reviewed Acme's note and proposed options. Short answer: we can approve a temporary HC waiver for customer-critical pilots under two constraints: (A) the role is explicitly timeboxed to 6 weeks with a handoff plan, (B) engineering signs off on minimal SLO impact.

I attached an updated org chart and a prefilled waiver form (acme-waiver-form-signed.pdf) to speed approvals. My proposal:
- Approve contractor engagement funded from a small contingency pool (mcp_costs.xlsx attached) for up to $24k total.
- Nominate an internal lead who can be backfilled by a 6-week contractor if needed.
- Require weekly status check-ins (Karthik to own) and a final readiness sign-off by Grace.

Rishi — can you confirm engineering can spare 0.8 FTE equivalent from existing workstreams for four weeks and 0.4 FTE for the remaining two? If so I will route the waiver and sign it off at People Ops.

Laura Bennett
Head of People Operations, Redwood Inference
Attachments: org-chart-v2.pdf, acme-waiver-form-signed.pdf, mcp_costs.xlsx
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: temporary coverage for Acme pilot onboarding

Thanks for the context. Confirming: engineering can provide the coverage with the following conditions — we will temporarily shift a senior IC (TBC) off a low-priority infra prototype for 4 weeks, then reduce to 0.4 FTE for weeks 5-6. We need:
1) a clear handoff document and daily overlap for first 3 business days,
2) written waiver (Laura — I see your signed form; please route to my attention),
3) a small budget reallocation for contractor overspill (Marissa to confirm).

I approve the waiver in principle provided the above are satisfied. Karthik, identify the lead and schedule a quick 30-min kick-off with Grace next week.

Rishi Malhotra
VP, Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Natalie Chen <natalie.chen@acmehealth.com>
Date: Sun, 7 Mar 2027 17:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: temporary coverage for Acme pilot onboarding

Looping back after finance looked at the numbers. We can absorb the $24k contingency from the customer pilot reserve (one-off). Finance asks for: (a) a signed waiver form in our HR tracking folder, (b) a brief 1-paragraph business case to attach to the spend, and (c) an expected close date for the pilot so we can mark the spend appropriately.

Karthik — can you confirm the start date (Mar 15 vs Mar 22) and send the 1-paragraph business case? I'll drop the waiver into HR once Laura confirms the sign-off and Rishi confirms the handoff plan.

Natalie — we'll aim to keep you on timeline; Karthik will confirm the resource and start date early next week.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

On Sun, Mar 7, 2027 at 08:02 AM, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi team — following up with a one-paragraph business case for finance and a proposed start:
>
> Business case (for finance): Acme Health pilot underpins a larger contract expected Q3 (est. $120k ARR). Delaying pilot by a month risks losing the procurement window and may defer expansion. Short-term contractor support (6 weeks) preserves timeline and enables on-time procurement close; contingency spend capped at $24k.
>
> Proposed start date: Mar 22 (allows 1 week for contractor ramp and overlap).
>
> Karthik
> Account Executive
> Redwood Inference
